name: Runner Extras - TableExt Eviction Field Trigger Timing
brief: Regression for issue #2463: RecordPatches.EvictCachedMetaTableForBaseTable dropped a base table's cached NCLMetaTable when a tableextension's fields merged in, but did not drop the table from _fieldTriggersWiredTables. The rebuilt NCLMetaTable's fields carried no ValidateHandler at all, so every field OnValidate body on that table silently stopped running for the rest of the process -- Validate(field, x) just set the field, with no error and no diagnostic.
description: The dependency app 'dep' declares table "Tefte T" (field 2 "Val" has an OnValidate trigger writing field 3 "Computed" := Val * 2) and an Install-subtype codeunit that materializes a "Tefte T" record during its OWN install -- forcing RecordPatches.WireFieldTriggerHandlersForTable to build+wire the table's NCLMetaTable via the standard `Record X` local-variable construction chokepoint, BEFORE this app's tableextension on "Tefte T" (adding field 4 "Extra") is even parsed. Once this app's AddSourceDir parses that tableextension, RecordPatches.MergeExtensionFields -> EvictCachedMetaTableForBaseTable evicts "Tefte T"'s already-built+wired NCLMetaTable so the next lookup rebuilds it with the extension field merged in. Before the fix, the table stayed marked 'already wired' in _fieldTriggersWiredTables across that rebuild, so the REBUILT NCLMetaTable's NCLMetaField for field 2 never got its ValidateHandler set -- Validate(Val, x) silently stopped running the field's OnValidate trigger, for a completely unrelated field on a table the extension never touched. This is the same 'wiring survives the table it was wired for' family as #2197/#2412 (table-level DB-trigger subscribers) and #2453 (TestPageFactory's record-construction chokepoint), here for the table's OWN compiled [FieldTriggerHandler] method rather than an event subscriber. This is a runner-internal caching defect, not a claim about BC behaviour, so it belongs in runner-extras rather than the upstream corpus.
